slides.say: Given: eight is smaller than x plus one, in absolute value. Which of the following cannot be the value of x?

Let's read it the other way round. Eight is smaller than the bars, so the bars are bigger than eight. They're on the big side. And look at the word cannot. We're looking for the one number that doesn't work. [short pause] We'll do it three ways.

[short pause] We need a distance from zero greater than eight. The whole inside can be far enough to the right or far enough to the left. Our first method, two cases. Big side means an open range, one part going to the right and one going to the left. So one option, the inside is bigger than eight. Take one off both sides, and x is bigger than seven.
at: one option, the inside is bigger

slides.say: For the left-hand case, the inside must lie beyond negative eight, farther away from zero. Or, the other option, the inside is smaller than negative eight. Now careful, the sign flips too, because now we're on the negative side. x plus one is smaller than negative eight, so x is smaller than negative nine.
at: the inside is smaller than negative eight

slides.say: So what does that leave? x can be above seven, or below negative nine, but not in between.

Nine and eleven are bigger than seven, so they can be x. Negative ten is smaller than negative nine, so it can be x too. And two? It's not above seven, and it's not below negative nine. It's stuck in the middle, so x cannot be two. Number two is our answer.

[pause] This time the fixed point is negative one. We're looking for all the points more than eight units away from it. Our second method, the number line. x plus one is the distance from negative one. More than eight steps from negative one means past seven on the right, or past negative nine on the left.
Two rays going outward, and a gap in the middle. Two is only three steps from negative one, and three isn't more than eight. So two sits in the gap, and it cannot be x. Number two.
[pause] Our third method, plugging in the answers. Nine plus one is ten, and ten is bigger than eight, so nine can be x.
Two plus one is three, and three is not bigger than eight. So two doesn't work. And in a cannot question, the one that doesn't work is the answer. In the exam you'd circle it and move on.

slides: [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
